sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a highly prevalent microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus. It is characterized by progressive damage to retinal capillaries, categorized primarily into Non-Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (NPDR) and Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (PDR) based on the presence of neovascularization (NV) triggered by retinal ischemia.

sections.title: Pathophysiology: The Ischemic Cascade
content: Step 1: Hyperglycemia leads to pericyte loss and basement membrane thickening.
Step 2: Microaneurysm formation and breakdown of the Blood-Retinal Barrier (BRB).
Step 3: Capillary closure and dropout resulting in retinal hypoxia.
Step 4: Upregulation of VEGF (Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor) due to hypoxia.
Step 5: Neovascularization (NV) at the disc (NVD) or elsewhere (NVE) defines the transition to PDR.

rows: More than MAs, but less than severe NPDR criteria
4-2-1 Rule: Intraretinal hemorrhages in 4 quadrants, Venous beading in 2, IRMA in 1
Presence of Neovascularization or Vitreous/Preretinal Hemorrhage

sections.title: Red Flags for PDR
content: Neovascularization of the Disc (NVD)
Tractional Retinal Detachment (TRD)
Vitreous Hemorrhage (VH)
Neovascular Glaucoma (NVG)
Presence of ghost vessels or fibrous proliferation

content.explanation: 4 quadrants of diffuse intraretinal hemorrhages/microaneurysms, 2 quadrants of venous beading, 1 quadrant of Intraretinal Microvascular Abnormalities (IRMA). Any one of these meets 'Severe', two meet 'Very Severe'.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy with 78D/90D lens.
Fundus Photography (7-field stereoscopic or ultra-widefield imaging).
Fluorescein Angiography (FFA) to identify non-perfusion areas and NV leakage.
OCT (Optical Coherence Tomography) to monitor for Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) and traction.
B-Scan Ultrasonography if media is opaque to rule out TRD.

sections.title: Management Protocol
content: Step 1: Metabolic Control (HbA1c optimization, BP control, lipid management).
Step 2: For DME: Anti-VEGF (Ranibizumab, Aflibercept) or intravitreal steroids (Dexamethasone implant).
Step 3: For PDR: Pan-Retinal Photocoagulation (PRP) is the gold standard.
Step 4: Surgical intervention (Pars Plana Vitrectomy) for non-clearing vitreous hemorrhage or TRD.
Step 5: Regular monitoring at 3-6 month intervals depending on severity.

sections.title: Recent Advances
content: Protocol S (DRCR.net): Found Anti-VEGF (Ranibizumab) non-inferior to PRP for visual acuity at 2 years.
Ultra-Widefield (UWF) Imaging: Identifies 'Peripheral Diabetic Retinopathy' not seen on standard 7-field imaging, correlating with higher progression risk.
Faricimab: Dual inhibition of Angiopoietin-2 and VEGF for longer durability.
